findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add acceptance-level tests that a simulated hard reconciler failure durably records the pass (via refs/reconciler/last-pass) despite the skipped commit-back step, and that the canary end-to-end consumes `status` from durable refs and escalates a ticket on staleness/failure — not merely that it stops calling the GHA API.
evidence: Tests named only for compatibility: 'Tests run both spellings against the same durable refs and assert equal results and no state mutation.'
AC5: 'A hard failure is still recorded despite the skipped commit-back step' — no corresponding test named.

AC7: 'The canary calls status and stops querying the GitHub Actions API for the heartbeat' — the cutover of the production channel, no end-to-end test that the canary reads durable state and files a ticket named.
findings.finding: The plan states tests only for the vocabulary-compatibility path (both spellings against the same durable refs, equal results, no mutation), but the two highest-stakes new behaviors — (1) a hard reconciler failure still producing the durable record despite the skipped commit-back step (AC5), and (2) the canary consuming `status` end-to-end and escalating via tickets on staleness/failure (AC7) — have no stated test. The failure-recording path is the exact inversion the plan calls out as the bug; without a test that a simulated hard failure writes refs/reconciler/last-pass, the suite can go green while the failure path stays broken.
findings.location: ## Vocabulary compatibility (tests) and Acceptance Criteria lines 5 and 7
scenarios: A reconciler hard-failure path is only asserted structurally or not at all, so the inverted-recording bug the plan sets out to fix could silently regress and close green.

The canary cutover is validated only by 'it no longer calls GHA API' rather than 'it escalates a real staleness/failure via a ticket from durable refs', leaving the production escalation path unexercised.
findings.suggested_fix: Add two AC-backed tests: one injecting a reconciler failure and asserting the durable ref carries failure_kind; one driving the canary against stale/failed durable refs and asserting a heartbeat-alert ticket is filed.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion that exercises the canary end-to-end: given a stale/failed durable status, it files the heartbeat-alert ticket.
evidence: 'escalates via tickets rather than being a parallel alarm' is described but no AC proves the escalation still fires from the new source
AC as written can pass while the ticket-filing path is broken
findings.finding: The canary escalation path is cut over to consuming status, but no acceptance criterion exercises end-to-end that a real staleness/failure surfaced by status actually produces a heartbeat-alert ticket — the ACs only assert the canary 'calls status' and stops the GHA API.
findings.location: AC 'The canary calls status and stops querying the GitHub Actions API for the heartbeat'
scenarios: The canary now reads status but a wiring bug means it never files a ticket on a stale/failed pass; all ACs pass green while production alerting is dead

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the full status tri-state and how each is derived: lock-present + fence-advancing-across-a-lease = running; lock-present + fence-stalled-across-a-lease = crashed; lock-absent + last-pass ref-blob = completed (with 'never ran' = both absent), and how the last-pass blob and the (at-rest absent) lock compose.
evidence: __main__.py:746-758 releases the lock in `finally` on BOTH the success and exception paths, so refs/reconciler/lock (and its fence) is absent once any pass ends
_ref_lock.py:517-558 try_break_if_stale reads (oid, fence) across one lease — this is the progress witness the plan reuses, but it only exists while the ref is present
Plan names crashed-vs-running via fence but does not enumerate the completed/at-rest state where the fence no longer exists
findings.finding: The status verdict's tri-state (completed vs running vs crashed) is under-specified: the lock ref — which carries the fence — is deleted in a `finally` on both success and failure, so the fence is only observable while a pass is in flight. The plan states the fence distinguishes crashed from running but never states how a cleanly-completed pass (lock absent, fence gone) is told apart from a never-ran state, nor how the always-pushed last-pass ref-blob composes with the now-absent lock at rest.
findings.location: Design paragraph ('Crashed vs running is answered by refs/reconciler/lock's FENCE') + AC 'Crashed is distinguished from running via the lock's fence across one lease'
scenarios: A pass completes cleanly, releases the lock; status runs and must report 'last run OK, nothing in flight' from the last-pass blob with NO lock present
A pass is SIGKILLed and never releases; status must read the stalled fence across a lease to say 'crashed'
findings.suggested_fix: State that status reads BOTH refs: the last-pass ref-blob for the completed-run summary and refs/reconciler/lock for in-flight state, and define the completed/running/crashed/never-ran matrix over {lock present?, fence advanced across one lease?, last-pass blob present?}.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify error handling/observability for the reconciler's ref push and status's ref read (retry/surface on push failure; defined canary behavior when the durable ref is unreachable).
evidence: The whole failure-capture guarantee rests on the ref push succeeding, yet no retry/backoff/error-surfacing for that push is described
No metric/log/alert for 'ref push failed' or 'status could not read the ref'
ABSENCE: nothing states what the canary does if the durable ref is unreachable
findings.finding: The new failure points introduced by the design — the reconciler pushing refs/reconciler/last-pass 'itself, not the workflow', and status fetching that ref — have no specified error handling or observability, so a failed ref push or fetch could silently break the always-pushed-truth guarantee.
findings.location: Design paragraph ('written by the reconciler process itself, not the workflow') + AC 'A hard failure is still recorded despite the skipped commit-back step'
scenarios: The reconciler crashes or loses network before pushing the ref during a hard failure — the failure is then recorded nowhere, silently inverting the guarantee just like the skipped commit-back it replaces
status cannot fetch the ref and the canary treats it as healthy (false negative) or errors (false positive)

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that the last-pass ref-blob and the lock fence are complementary durability signals — the blob records outcomes for passes that reached their write point (including handled hard failures), while a crash BEFORE the write is surfaced by the abandoned lock's stalled fence — and that a hard failure recorded via the blob requires the reconciler to push it on the failure path.
evidence: A ref push requires the process to run to the push point; __main__.py:738-745 catches exceptions and returns 1, but a SIGKILL/OOM leaves no push at all
The plan's own trap analysis notes the commit-back is skipped on reconciler failure — but distinguishes only workflow-skip, not process-death-before-write
findings.finding: The 'minimal always-pushed truth' is only pushed if the reconciler process reaches its write point; a crash before the push (SIGKILL/OOM/startup failure) writes no last-pass ref-blob. The plan presents the ref-blob as the durability answer to the skipped commit-back, but the abandoned-lock/fence signal is the actual mechanism for a crash-before-write. The plan does not state that these two signals are complementary and which covers which failure class.
findings.location: Design paragraph ('a ref-blob refs/reconciler/last-pass carries the minimal always-pushed truth') + AC 'A hard failure is still recorded despite the skipped commit-back step'
scenarios: acli auth fails at pass startup, process never reaches the last-pass write — the only durable trace is the (possibly never-acquired) lock
Runner OOM-kills the process mid-pass; lock is held with a stalled fence, no last-pass blob written

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the commit-back premise: cite reconcile-bridge.yml:313 (not :272) and state precisely that the step's existing `if: steps.reconcile.outputs.paused != 'true'` is not `failure()`/`always()`-guarded, so GHA skips it when the reconcile step exits non-zero — rather than that it 'has no if: condition'.
evidence: .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml:272 is 'set +e'; the commit step is at 313 with 'if: steps.reconcile.outputs.paused != 'true''
The real mechanism is that the existing if: lacks failure()/always(), so GHA skips it when the reconcile step exits non-zero (line 310 'exit "$rc"') — not that the step is unconditional
findings.finding: The plan asserts 'the commit-back step has no if: condition (reconcile-bridge.yml:272)', but reconcile-bridge.yml:272 is 'set +e' inside the reconcile step, and the actual commit-back step ('Commit reconciler events back and push to origin/tickets', line 313) DOES carry an if: (if: steps.reconcile.outputs.paused != 'true'). The premise as literally stated is refuted by the file, and the cited line is wrong.
findings.location: Plan § 'And the commit-back step has no if: condition' / .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml:313
scenarios: An implementer trusting the premise removes/adds an if: at line 272 (wrong location) and does not touch the real step at 313
Reviewer cannot reconcile the 'no if:' claim with the file and loses confidence in the failure-recording design
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to: 'the commit-back step (reconcile-bridge.yml:313) is gated only on `paused != 'true'`; because that `if:` is not `always()`/`failure()`, GHA skips it whenever the reconciler step exits non-zero, so a committed-only record silently drops every hard failure.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the commit-back step citation (it is reconcile-bridge.yml:313 with `if: steps.reconcile.outputs.paused != 'true'`, not line 272 with no condition) and restate the actual failure-skip behavior it exhibits.

reconcile-bridge.yml:272 is `set +e`
reconcile step sets outputs.paused only on rc==0 (line 279 `if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]`)

findings.location: Plan intro: 'And the commit-back step has no if: condition (reconcile-bridge.yml:272)'; AC 'A hard failure is still recorded despite the skipped commit-back step'
